body:
Hey. The same thing happened to us. Same error in the log:
pm2 has been killed by signal, dumping process list before exit

When we checked all of our services suddenly disappeared from the pm2 list.
Really weird.

Wondering if anyone might have an explanation for that.

Hi there,

I think one possible reason for receiving multiple SIGTERM signals is to have multiple pm2 daemon running. So each of them receive signals but they read/write into the same dump file.

In any case, we can't really find all possible reasons, and some of them are out of pm2 scope (imagine if you use a buggy script that send multiple SIGTERM to pm2).

To me, the best thing to do is to stop signal listening after the first SIGTERM is received.
Then listen signal again when all processes are killed.

So good to see this, I was just about to report it after seeing some apps arbitrarily not restart after reboot on a server that has 57 apps. This same setup worked ok for us for a year in the same setup on Ubuntu 14.04 but when we moved to 18.04 a month ago we started having this issue on reboot. Verified that we only have one PM2 daemon running still had the issue.

Looking forward to this release.

Hi @LilMinmax 

You gave us great information. It seems problem come from Ubuntu since issue occurred only after upgrading.
Maybe for some reason ubuntu 18 send many SIGTERM to pm2.

In any case PR #3876 should fix it.
